# Proto-Gospel of James Chapter 19 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Bodmer V / Greek MSS, Proto-Gospel of James 19 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/POX_019_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 19

**19:1** And they stood at the entrance to the cave, and behold, a luminous cloud overshadowed the cave. The midwife said: "My soul is magnified today, because my eyes have seen wonderful things — for salvation has been born to Israel." And immediately the cloud withdrew from the cave, and a great light appeared inside, so that their eyes could not bear it. And little by little the light withdrew until the infant was visible. And he went and took the breast of his mother Mary.

**19:2** And the midwife cried out: "This day is great for me, for I have seen a new sight."

**19:3** And the midwife came out from the cave, and Salome met her. The midwife said to her: "Salome, Salome, I have a new sight to tell you. A virgin has brought forth, which her nature does not allow."

**19:4** And Salome said: "As the Lord my God lives, unless I insert my finger and examine her condition, I will not believe that a virgin has brought forth."

**19:5** And the midwife went in and said to Mary: "Brace yourself, for no small controversy has arisen concerning you." And Salome came in and examined her condition. And she cried out, saying: "Woe to me for my iniquity and my unbelief! I have tempted the living God, and behold, my hand is falling away from me in fire!"

**19:6** And Salome knelt before the Lord, saying: "O God of my fathers, remember me, for I am the seed of Abraham and Isaac and Jacob. Do not make me an example before the children of Israel, but restore me to the poor, for you know, Lord, that in your name I have performed my services, and I have received my wage from you."

**19:7** And behold, an angel of the Lord stood before her and said: "Salome, Salome, the Lord God has heard your prayer. Bring your hand to the infant and take him up, and you will have salvation and joy."

**19:8** And Salome came near and took him up, saying: "I will worship him, for a great king has been born to Israel." And immediately Salome was healed, and she went out from the cave justified, glorifying and praising God. And behold, a voice came to her: "Salome, Salome, tell not the marvels you have seen until the child has come into Jerusalem."

---

## Translator's Note

Chapter 19 is the theological and dramatic climax of the Protevangelium. The sequence — cloud, blinding light, gradual dimming, infant at the breast — presents the birth as a theophany identical in pattern to the Sinai revelation (cloud, fire, divine presence). The midwife's words "My soul is magnified" (19:1) echo Anna (5:3) and the Magnificat. The Salome episode is a direct model for the Doubting Thomas narrative (John 20:24-29): doubt expressed, examination demanded, physical contact with the sacred, punishment/healing, confession. The burned/healed hand became one of the most frequently depicted scenes in Byzantine Nativity iconography.
